name: Title
text: Hi! We're Group 14, Team Sweet Potatoes.

name: Title
text: We studied how international residents in Melbourne take part in council decisions.

name: Five problems
text: Our investigation found five problems.

name: Five problems
text: One: even when it's translated, council language is hard to understand.

name: Five problems
text: Two: time, distance and fees keep people from attending.

name: Five problems
text: Three: people only take part when an issue feels personally relevant.

name: Five problems
text: Four: they don't know which department to contact, or whether they were heard.

name: Five problems
text: Five: council news arrives by mail and flyers, but newer residents live on Instagram.

name: Persona & scenario
text: Let's meet Jason.

name: Persona & scenario
text: He's 34, has lived in Melbourne for eight years, and English isn't his first language.

name: Persona & scenario
text: One Saturday morning, a new park rule limits when his dog can be off the leash.

name: Persona & scenario
text: He disagrees, but doesn't know who to tell, or which words to use.

name: Introducing HearHere
text: So we introduce HearHere: a digital device that combines a physical information pillar with an AI customised helper.

name: Introducing HearHere
text: Hi there! I'm Spud, the Street Post for Understanding Decisions.

name: Introducing HearHere
text: Here's the post from every side.

name: How it works
text: It connects three channels. Spud's official account shares only verified council posts, where residents already scroll.

name: How it works
text: An AI agent answers questions, and the HearHere app tracks each issue.

name: Discover
text: Back to Saturday, 8 a.m. Jason walks his dog past a HearHere post.

name: Discover
text: Its pillar shows verified council and community notices.

name: Discover
text: Hi! Got something to say? I'm all ears.

name: Discover
text: The screen under Spud lists nearby issues by distance, including a new rule for the park next door.

name: Understand & speak
text: Jason taps the park issue.

name: Understand & speak
text: A plain-language summary appears in his own language, with difficult terms explained.

name: Understand & speak
text: Now he simply talks to Spud, in his own language.

name: Understand & speak
text: The new park rule makes walking my dog really inconvenient. I hope it can be reconsidered.

name: Understand & speak
text: Spud turns it into a clear English comment, names the responsible department, and lets Jason edit before sending.

name: Understand & speak
text: No audio is stored.

name: NFC & tracking
text: Jason taps his phone on the NFC pad.

name: NFC & tracking
text: The issue and his comment move to the HearHere app, and the post keeps nothing.

name: NFC & tracking
text: Tracking begins only because Jason chose it.

name: NFC & tracking
text: The app shows each stage: Received, In review, then an outcome with a case number, or reasons if declined.

name: NFC & tracking
text: Each new HearHere post Jason visits also earns a badge: a small reward for taking part.

name: Share
text: Jason can also share the issue as a card on Instagram, so his neighbours can join in.

name: Benefits
text: For Jason, that means relevant issues on his route, in his own language, a clear department, and visible progress.

name: Benefits
text: All without attending a meeting.

name: Limits & next steps
text: HearHere has limits.

name: Limits & next steps
text: Speaking in public may feel exposing, AI can mistranslate, and our fieldwork didn't include council staff.

name: Limits & next steps
text: Next, we'll test a low-fidelity prototype with residents across languages.

name: Tagline
text: HearHere, with Spud: the Street Post for Understanding Decisions.

name: Tagline
text: Speak here. Be heard!
